title: Plant DNA Extraction Using Qiagen Genomic Tip
author: CHIARA NATALI
materials: Proceed to next section of the protocol.

Equilibrate a QIAGEN Genomic-tip with 10 ml of Buffer QBT, and allow the QIAGEN Genomic-tip to empty by gravity flow. Place a QIAGEN Genomic-tip over a tube using a tip holder or into a QIArack over the waste tray. Equilibrate the QIAGEN Genomic-tip with 10 ml of Buffer QBT described above. Flow begins automatically by reduction in surface tension due to the presence of detergent (0.15% Triton X-100) in the equilibration buffer. Allow the QIAGEN Genomic-tip to drain completely. The flow of buffer will stop when the meniscus reaches the upper frit. The frit prevents the QIAGEN Genomic-tip from running dry, allowing it to be left unattended. Do not force out the remaining buffer, as this will necessitate restarting the flow with a syringe and adapter. The binding, washing, and elution conditions for QIAGEN resin are strongly influenced by pH.

The cleared lysate is loaded onto a pre-equilibrated QIAGEN Genomic-tip by gravity flow. The salt and pH conditions of the lysate and the superior selectivity of the QIAGEN resin ensure that only DNA binds, while degraded RNA, cellular proteins, and metabolites are not retained and appear in the flow-through fraction. Vortexing the genomic DNA has a minimal effect on the size of the DNA, and it accelerates the QIAGEN procedure by eliminating poor flow rates associated with clogging. Vortex the sample (from step 9) for 10 seconds at maximum speed and apply it to the equilibrated QIAGEN Genomic-tip. Allow it to enter the resin by gravity flow. The sample should be loaded onto the QIAGEN Genomic-tip promptly. If left too long, it may become cloudy due to further precipitation of protein. The sample must then be centrifuged or filtered before loading to prevent clogging of the QIAGEN Genomic-tip. Once the QIAGEN Genomic-tip is loaded with the clear and particle-free sample, flow will begin unassisted. Allow gravity to determine the flow rate. Particularly concentrated genomic DNA lysates may exhibit diminished flow rates due to increased viscosity. It may also be helpful to dilute the lysate with an equal volume of Buffer QBT prior to loading.

The QIAGEN Genomic-tip is then washed with a medium-salt buffer (Buffer QC). This buffer completely removes any remaining contaminants, such as traces of RNA and protein (e.g., RNase A), without affecting the binding of the DNA. Buffer QC also disrupts nonspecific interactions and allows removal of nucleic acid-binding proteins without the use of phenol. The low concentration of ethanol in the wash buffer eliminates nonspecific hydrophobic interactions, further enhancing the purity of the boundDNA. Wash the QIAGEN Genomic-tip with 2 x 15 ml of Buffer QC. Allow Buffer QC to move through the QIAGEN Genomic-tip by gravity flow. Two washes are sufficient to remove all contaminants in the majority of DNA preparations. It is particularly important not to force out residual Buffer QC. Traces of Buffer QC will not affect the elution step.

The DNA is then efficiently eluted from the QIAGEN Genomic-tip with a high-salt buffer (Buffer QF). The eluted DNA is desalted and concentrated by isopropanol precipitation. Precipitation is carried out at room temperature (15-25°C) to minimize coprecipitation of salt. After centrifugation, the DNA pellet is washed with 70% ethanol to remove residual salt and to replace the isopropanol with ethanol, which is more volatile and easily removed. Use of Buffer QF pre-warmed to 50°C will increase yields.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Grind Leaf Material
steps.instruction: Grind 1–2 g of leaf material in liquid nitrogen using a mortar and pestle.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Mixture
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue powder into a 50 ml screw-cap tube and add lysis reagents.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 ml of Carlson lysis buffer (100 mM Tris·Cl pH 9.5, 2% CTAB, 1.4 M NaCl, 1% PEG 6000 or 8000, 20 mM EDTA) pre-warmed to 74°C
Add 25 µl β-mercaptoethanol
Add 100 µl of RNase A (20 mg/ml)
Vortex at full speed for 5–10 s

steps.title: Incubate Samples
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at 74°C for 20 minutes in a shaking water bath.

substeps.instruction: If a shaking water bath is unavailable, gently shake samples every 5 min

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the DNA from proteins and lipids using chloroform/isoamyl alcohol.

substeps.instruction: Cool samples to room temperature
Add 1 volume of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (24:1)
Vortex at full speed for 5–10 seconds
Centrifuge at 5,000 x g for 10 minutes at 4°C
Transfer the aqueous upper phase to a fresh 50 ml screw-cap tube

steps.title: Adjust pH
steps.instruction: Adjust the pH of the aqueous phase to 7.0.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 volume of distilled water
Adjust pH to 7.0 using HCl (generally 100–200 µl of 25% HCl is required)

steps.title: Prepare Genomic-tip
steps.instruction: Place the QIAGEN Genomic-tip over a clean 30 ml collection tube (do not use polycarbonate centrifuge tubes).

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Elute the DNA from the tip using Buffer QF.

substeps.instruction: Elute with 1 x 15 ml of Buffer QF
Allow the tip to drain by gravity flow to collect the eluate

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Precipitate the DNA from the eluate using isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 10.5 ml (0.7 volumes) of room-temperature (15–25°C) isopropanol to the eluted DNA
Mix and centrifuge immediately at >5000 x g for at least 15 minutes at 4°C
Carefully remove the supernatant with a pipet

steps.title: Wash DNA Pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the precipitated DNA pellet to remove salts.

substeps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 4 ml of cold 70% ethanol (a second wash may be performed for sensitive applications)
Vortex briefly
Centrifuge at >5000 x g for 10 minutes at 4°C

steps.title: Dry and Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Dry the pellet and dissolve the DNA in a suitable buffer.

substeps.instruction: Briefly dry the pellet by vacuum centrifuge (avoid overdrying)
Resuspend in 0.1-2 ml of suitable buffer (e.g., TE buffer pH 8.0, or 10 mM Tris·Cl pH 8.5)
Dissolve the DNA overnight on a shaker at room temperature; avoid pipetting up and down to prevent shearing

steps.title: Quantify and Analyze DNA
steps.instruction: Determine the yield, purity, and size distribution of the extracted DNA.

substeps.instruction: Measure concentration and purity (A260/A280 and A260/A230) via spectrophotometry (Pure DNA: A260/A280 1.7-1.9, A260/A230 2.0-2.2)
For precise concentration, measure a 1 µl aliquot with a Qubit fluorometer using the 1X dsDNA HS kit
Resolve size distribution using Pippin Pulse Gel Electrophoresis with 50-100 ng of gDNA and Quick-Load 1 kb Extend DNA Ladder (0.5 kb to 48.5 kb)
